title: Pin model variants and publish performance profiles: update catalog schema + docs
creator: Asha Patel
description: Add a stable, auditable version pinning field to model catalog metadata and publish machine-readable performance profiles for newly onboarded models. This ticket covers schema changes, ingestion pipeline updates, SDK/API surface changes, and doc updates so customers can reliably pin to a model version and see SKU-level latency/cost/quality profiles.
background: Customers have asked for clear controls to lock inference to a specific model binary and to see performance trade-offs (latency, cost, memory, quality) before they migrate production traffic. Current catalog entries are loosely versioned and lack an explicit pinned_versions property and a standardized performance_profile blob. New models (internal name 'cerberus') are ready for onboarding and we need the infra and docs to support pinning + profile publishing.
tasks: Extend catalog JSON schema: add 'pinned_versions' (list) and 'performance_profiles' (list of profiles) with schema versioning
Update onboarding ingestion lambda to populate pinned_versions automatically from model registry tags
Implement a streaming job to generate and store standardized performance profiles (latency P50/P95, tokens/sec, VRAM footprint, quantization impact)
Expose pinned_versions and performance_profiles in the public API and SDK (Python/JS) with feature flagging
Add Console UI: model detail page shows pin selector, compare profiles UI, and link to pin rollout guide
Write docs and quickstart: how to pin, how pin interacts with routing/fallbacks, recommended pinning strategies
Backfill pinned_versions for models onboarded in last 6 months where possible and annotate missing data
Add end-to-end tests for schema compatibility and an API contract test for performance_profiles
Coordinate rollout with product: deprecate ambiguous 'version' field in favor of pinned_versions over next two quarters
acceptance_criteria: Catalog schema v2 released with pinned_versions and performance_profiles fields documented
Ingestion pipeline populates pinned_versions for new model uploads by default
Performance profiles generated and visible in model detail API responses for 'cerberus-v2' and at least 2 other recent onboardings
SDKs return pin-able model metadata and include example code in docs
Console surfaces pin control and profile comparison UI behind a feature flag
API contract tests pass in CI and catalog-2026.03 release notes include the migration plan
progress_updates: 2026-03-10: Kickoff meeting with product and design. Agreed schema names and profile metrics (p50,p95,tokens_per_sec,peak_vram,quantized_delta,eval_agreement).
2026-03-11: Implemented initial schema changes in branch feature/catalog-schema-v2. Added pinned_versions as an array of strings. Opened PR #1423.

2026-03-12: Ingestion lambda change reviewed by infra. Noted edge case: model registries that only publish 'nightly' tags — decided to record both tag and created_at as part of ingestion (created_at persisted in separate field already).
2026-03-13: Generated perf profile job PoC for cerberus-v2. Early numbers: quantized-int8 reduces peak_vram by ~45% with ~1.1x latency at P95; need to normalize measurement harness.
review_feedback: PM (Lena Ortiz): prefer 'pinned_versions' to be ordered by recommended stability (most stable first).
Design (Mikhail Kovalenko): Console should show a clear CTA and explain rollback behavior when pinning is applied.
Security (Grace Liu): ensure performance_profiles do not leak internal node identifiers or IPs — confirmed profiles will be aggregated and anonymized.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Customers may rely on floating 'latest' semantics; pinning could be confusing. Mitigation: Add explicit warnings and migration doc + default to not pin existing apps.

Risk: Performance profile variability across hardware may create noisy data. Mitigation: Publish profiles broken out by hardware class (A100-40GB, A10G, etc.) and include sampling windows and seed prompts for reproducibility.
Risk: Schema change breaks older SDKs. Mitigation: Serve schema version in API and keep backward-compatible v1 responses for two quarters.
Risk: Large backfill costs. Mitigation: Backfill lazily on first model detail request for older models and prioritize top-n customer models.
open_questions: Should pinned_versions include both semantic version and build hash or only the build hash? (Trade-off: semantics vs. opaque stability)
How to represent multi-variant bundles (float16 + int8) as a single catalog entry?
Do we need an audit trail when a customer pins/unpins a model (for Private deployments we must) and should that be part of this ticket or a follow-up?
next_steps: Address review comments on PR #1423 and land catalog schema changes
Finish perf-harness normalization and attach reproducibility artifacts to perf profiles
Create SDK changes RFC and small PRs to read pinned_versions from API
Schedule UX review for Console pin UI and plan small canary with internal customers
